scope.description: Bounded local provider and billing runtime fixes with disposable PostgreSQL evidence.

candidate.digestAlgorithm: SHA-256 of sorted relative-path\0byte-size\0file-digest entries joined with LF; lockfile is raw byte SHA-256

independence: The reviewer inspected implementation and evidence, reproduced negative validator cases, independently reran focused tests and computed evidence checks. The reviewer did not edit implementation, tests, schemas, the runner, or acceptance records; only these independent review artifacts were written.

billingReconciliationProbe.profile: privileged disposable PostgreSQL 17.6 at 127.0.0.1:55432 with fixture provider

databaseProbe.profile: privileged disposable PostgreSQL 17.6 at 127.0.0.1:55432 with fixture provider
cases: verified payment persists inbox and issues one catalog grant
verified duplicate webhook is acknowledged without a second effect
invoice and PaymentIntent aliases converge on the original order and grant
failed webhook delivery is retryable with the same event identity after the transient prerequisite is restored
stale received inbox rows are reclaimed after the lease and converge without a duplicate grant
aliases are resolved as exact provider/object/id tuples and cannot cross-pair two orders
known canonical orders reject mismatched workspace and customer hints before any account lock or financial effect
forged signature has no durable financial or inbox effect
refund-before-payment holds the workspace and late payment cannot grant credits

officialSchemaRecheck.method: Independent read-only HTTP GET to manifest official URLs; extract exact selected Replicate version schema or fal OpenAPI JSON, serialize with two-space JSON plus LF, and recompute SHA-256.

findings.evidence: payment-aliases.ts queries each provider/objectKind/externalId tuple; probe case 'aliases are resolved as exact provider/object/id tuples and cannot cross-pair two orders'.

reconcile-payment.ts checks workspaceId and customerId hints against the canonical order before account lock; probe case 'known canonical orders reject mismatched workspace and customer hints before any account lock or financial effect'.
inbox.ts resets failed rows and retries with the same delivery identity; probe case 'failed webhook delivery is retryable with the same event identity after the transient prerequisite is restored'.
inbox.ts uses a row lock and 60-second received lease; probe case 'stale received inbox rows are reclaimed after the lease and converge without a duplicate grant'.

invariants: Canonical workspace and customer hint consistency before account lock
Failed webhook redelivery retry with stable event identity
Stale received inbox lease recovery with row locking

limits: PASS is limited to local fixture contracts and disposable PostgreSQL evidence.
No Stripe account, live fal request, production billing, production email, paid request, or external network evidence was used.
This review does not approve the M4 or M5 stage gate and does not alter task or stage status.
decisionSummary: The bounded local implementation contracts for M4 task 5.3 and M5 tasks 6.3/6.4 pass independent review. Exact payment alias tuples, canonical workspace/customer consistency, failed webhook retry, and stale received lease recovery are covered by source inspection and a privileged nine-case disposable PostgreSQL probe.
